items.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024
items.q: Dick Bock started the Pacific Jazz Record Company to record that group and immediately started to record them...

ctx.x: I had the same experience, you know at SUNY Fredonia. He came there and I was star- struck and I kept thinking that’s what I want to do. I want to be in a band like that. And as it turns out, you know, I’m more of a Basie guy. But still, there’s nothing like that. I’m wondering if, in all your research that you’ve done about different people, especially on the West Coast, and you read what other people write about them, and then you get to know the actual person and you have conversations about them. Have you…

Many times. Many times. Because as you know the West Coast scene of the ‘50s, by the end of the ‘50s there was a definite turning point within the critics and people writing about it where that music was very much dismissed and artists associated with that music got a lot of negative press as well. And so then I would — as doing the research, and you would read things, like you said, you would read these interviews and things about certain artists that just didn’t — when I would meet them and get to know them it…

taskmaster. But you would read about the things people had written and a lot of times it just didn’t match up with the person that I had gotten to know. And over the years I would get to know many of those guys on a pretty close level. Because the type of events, the type of things that I was doing kind of required working closely with them, working closely with them on the music, things like that. And then once you can kind of — the other things that I’m proud of is that I had stayed in — you know I was in music…
